city.Botswana.flag: sky blue with a black-and-white stripe across the middle
city.Botswana.clue.0: boasted about seeing more elephants than anywhere else in the world
city.Burkina Faso.description: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa whose name means “Land of Upright People.” It is one of the world's top gold producers, and fields of cotton stretch across its farmland.
city.Burkina Faso.landmark: mud-brick Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso bristling with wooden support beams
city.Burkina Faso.flag: red on top, green below, with a single yellow star in the middle
city.Burkina Faso.clue.0: planned a trip to a landlocked patch of West Africa known for gold and fields of cotton
city.Burkina Faso.clue.1: couldn't stop talking about a land whose name means 'home of honest, upright people'
city.Burkina Faso.clue.2: planned to visit mines where workers dig for glittering gold
city.Burkina Faso.clue.3: was curious about the mysterious ruins of an old stone fortress
city.Burundi.description: Burundi is a small, hilly country in East Africa near the great lakes. Cattle are treasured here as a sign of respect, and almost everyone shares the same language, called Kirundi.
city.Burundi.landmark: drummers in white-and-green robes performing on a green hillside above Lake Tanganyika
city.Burundi.flag: a white diagonal cross (an X) splitting it into red and green, with three red stars in the center
city.Burundi.clue.0: wanted to watch hippos and crocodiles where a river spills out onto the plains
city.Burundi.clue.1: kept talking about a place where cows are prized as a sign of great respect
city.Cabo Verde.description: This string of ten volcanic islands sits in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa. It is famous for sunny beaches, steady trade winds, salt scraped from an old crater, and lively music.
city.Cabo Verde.landmark: towering cone of the Pico do Fogo volcano rising above black-lava vineyards
city.Cabo Verde.greeting: Most people speak Cape Verdean Creole and Portuguese — say hello with “Olá” (oh-LAH).
city.Cabo Verde.flag: deep blue with a ring of ten little yellow stars and a band of white and red
city.Cabo Verde.clue.0: kept talking about heading to a cluster of islands far out in the Atlantic, off the coast of West Africa
city.Cabo Verde.clue.1: wanted to see the pale beaches and salt pans where sea salt is scraped from inside an old volcano crater
city.Cameroon.description: Nicknamed “Africa in miniature,” Cameroon packs deserts, rainforests, mountains, and a coastline into one country. Up north, the Waza reserve is a great place to spot lions and giraffes.
city.Cameroon.landmark: Lobé Waterfalls tumbling straight into the ocean surf
city.Cameroon.greeting: People speak French and English here — say hello in French with “Bonjour” (bawn-ZHOOR).
city.Cameroon.flag: three tall stripes of green, red, and yellow with a single yellow star in the middle
city.Cameroon.clue.0: called the place “Africa in miniature” because it has deserts, rainforests, mountains, and beaches all in one country
city.Cameroon.clue.1: planned a safari up north to look for lions and giraffes on a dry, dusty reserve
city.Cameroon.clue.2: pored over photos of kings' beaded masks and carved wooden thrones from old mountain kingdoms
city.Central African Republic.descriptio: This landlocked country sits right in the middle of Africa. Its Dzanga-Sangha rainforest shelters forest elephants and gorillas, and the Boali Falls tumble down a river near the capital.
